records.wording: NA27. The Marcionite speaker in the Dialogue sets the saying against Elisha and the bears (2 Kgs 2:23–24) in an antithesis. His "kingdom of the heavens" is Matthew's; "come to me" is Luke's wording. Tertullian knows a similar antithesis but sets it against Matt 18:3–4 (4.23.4). The attestation is weak, and Roth rates the wording possible only.

records.wording: NA27 "one, God" printed by method (METHOD §11) against the attested Marcionite reading "God the Father" (ὁ θεὸς ὁ πατήρ). Epiphanius says that Marcion "added 'the Father'"; the Dialogue and Origen's report of the heretics' use also have "the Father"; Roth: very likely. Tertullian has only "God", and Roth allows that the copies differed. The correspondential reading marks the addition as a strain: it turns into an outward title, set against "me", the relation the text keeps open and gives only by revealing (10:22); NA27 continues the line (the one good, the one thing lacking, "follow me", 18:22). On the premise of a correspondential original the addition belongs to the transmission of Marcion's copies, as Tertullian's copy without it suggests (docs/research/correspondence/word_by_word.md, chapter 16; second_pass.md §3). Epiphanius' "do not call me good" and "one is good" are rated probable only; NA27 is printed for the rest.

records.wording: Marcionite reading adopted: the order "do not kill, do not commit adultery" (Tertullian; the Dialogue), with μηδέ before the last prohibition (the Dialogue); Roth: very likely. It is the order of the Hebrew Decalogue, Matthew 19:18 and almost every Old Latin manuscript of Luke. Epiphanius has "I know the commandments" (spoken by the man); Tertullian and the Dialogue have "you know". Roth: the copies may have differed. NA27 "you know" is printed.
records.western: The order kill–adultery is that of the Old Latin.

records.wording: Marcionite readings adopted: no "still" (ἔτι) before "one thing you lack", δός ("give") for διάδος ("distribute"), and ἐν οὐρανῷ ("in heaven", singular) for NA27's ἐν [τοῖς] οὐρανοῖς. Tertullian quotes the verse and repeats its parts; the Dialogue agrees. Roth: secure. δός is the reading of ℵ A D L and others, ἐν οὐρανῷ of W Θ Ψ f1.13 and the Byzantine text (NA27 apparatus).

records.reason: The camel and the needle, and the reward of those who left everything: a separate NA27 paragraph with no attested verse (METHOD §4.3). Tertullian passes from 18:23 (4.36.5) to 18:35 (4.36.8–9). The Dialogue of Adamantius refers to 18:24–30, but not from Marcion's text (Harnack, Roth).

records.reason: Class A−: Epiphanius (sch. 52) states that the whole third prediction of the passion, with "everything written by the prophets about the son of man will be fulfilled", was not in the text. Tertullian passes from 18:23 to 18:35; Roth counts his silence as confirmation (tacitus). Restored by method (METHOD §11): by its words, the restored 24:44 says "these are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that everything written (πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα) about me… must be fulfilled", and no printed saying to the disciples contains it except 18:31, "everything written (πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα) through the prophets about the son of man will be accomplished", said to the twelve. By its mechanics: the restored 24:45 "he opened their mind to understand (συνιέναι)" lifts the veil that 18:34 lays ("they understood (συνῆκαν) none of these things… this saying was hidden from them"). Reading: docs/research/correspondence/second_pass.md §4. Printed against Marcion's text: the witness states that the passage was not in it.
